text:
iris: lowering the threshold - we just saw continuous-batch + kv-cache explode on tp-kv pool, GPUs started NCCL AllGather stalls and paging spiked. declaring incident. 1959993333
incidents-bot: INCIDENT CREATED #1959993333 - kv-cache/paging spike on tp-kv (priority P1) - paging I/O increase, elevated GPU memory swaps, potential customer impact. runbook: /runbooks/kv-cache-paging.md :rotating_light: 
jake: i'm oncall, pinged maya to take handoff, putting channel in read-only for updates. can someone post the quick metrics?
maya: jumping in — p95 latency for hosted-generation routes jumped from ~120ms -> ~2.4s over last 6m, tail tokens/sec collapsed. db paging read/s increased 20x, iostat shows heavy random reads on nvme. NCCL logs show repeated "AllGather timed out" messages on rank 2/3.
iris: noticed continuous_batch.size kept auto-increasing because prefix caching entries were never evicted due to sharding bug. cache growth -> OOM -> fallback to disk -> paging.
prod-support: customer-impact: 3 paying customers (org: enterprise-alpha, beta-inc, gameloft-labs) reported 503s / timeouts for generation calls. we've opened tickets and informed CS.
customer-success: emailing alpha contact with status, they saw degraded throughput and hallucination rate increase (timeouts caused retries).
jake: mitigation plan from runbook: 1) disable continuous_batch autoscale 2) cap continuous_batch.max_tokens to 1024 3) set kv_cache.shard_strategy = "legacy" (no-tp-round-robin) 4) roll a tensor-parallel hotfix to prevent uneven key partitioning 5) canary patch to 5% then 25% then 100%. doing steps 1-3 now.
maya: running command to set live config via controlplane api: ```
# temporarily cap batching and disable autoscale
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/configs/live -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"continuous_batch.autoscale":false,"continuous_batch.max_tokens":1024,"kv_cache.shard_strategy":"legacy"}'
```
deploy-bot: CONFIG UPDATE initiated by maya at 1959993440: continuous_batch.autoscale=false, continuous_batch.max_tokens=1024, kv_cache.shard_strategy=legacy - applied to pool tp-kv-canary (10% instances)
jake: okay, monitoring. can we get a snapshot of NCCL error counts and page-fault rate?
maya: `kubectl logs -lapp=tp-kv -c runtime --since=10m | grep NCCL | wc -l` -> 124 errors in last 10m on canary nodes. /metrics shows gpu_page_faults/sec = 48 -> down from 120 after config change on canary. latency p95 on canary reduced to 210ms.
iris: big signal: imbalance in keyspace partitioning - rank 2 owns 42% of keys because of hash mismatch introduced in last tensor-parallel gearbox change (commit: a1b2c3f). that created hot shard and caused repeated kv-cache growth.
prod-support: continuing to route critical customers to standby region with smaller model to keep SLAs during mitigation. traffic flip 15% -> standby-region.
maya: preparing hotfix PR to correct partition hashing and add a safety cap (max_keys_per_shard). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/2298 - patch includes unit tests and an opt-in feature flag.
jake: we prefer an emergency patch with no feature flag for rollout speed, but safety cap should be default. can we hotpatch runtime image with just the cap and hashing fix?
maya: yes, building image now. quick build: ```
# build and tag emergency image
make -C runtime build-image IMAGE_TAG=emergency-1959993445
docker push registry.redwood/emergency-1959993445
```
deploy-bot: HOTPATCH IMAGE pushed and scheduled for canary deploy at 1959993590 (10% nodes). healthchecks: readiness probe 10s, rollback on >3 failing pods.
iris: after canary, observed NCCL stall errors drop 85%, page faults down to baseline on canary. p95 for canary routes ~130ms. starting staged rollout to remaining tp-kv nodes.
jake: do not forget to increase eviction aggressiveness in kv-cache: set eviction.min_age to 30s while we stabilize.
maya: applied eviction.min_age=30s live. monitoring GC churn.
prod-support: customers alpha and beta reported recovery, gameloft still seeing occasional spikes — routing 100% of their traffic to standby region for now.
iris: root cause hypothesis: recent TP gearbox change (a1b2c3f) changed key hashing mapping during shard rebalancing; combined with continuous-batch autoscale that assumed uniform key distribution -> key concentration + infinite cache retention -> memory blowout -> OOM -> fallback paging -> NCCL AllGather timeouts due to uneven NVLink traffic.
jake: action items: 1) emergency hotfix rolled to prod (done) 2) rollback autoscale default to off until safeties merged (done) 3) postmortem ticket with timeline and impact 4) add unit/integration test for key-distribution invariants 5) add alert for kv-shard-skew > 2x 6) retro on runbook gaps. assigning owners.
iris: creating the postmortem ticket now -> https://issues.redwood/INC-1959993333-postmortem assigned to maya and jake.
customer-success: update: alpha and beta satisfied with interim mitigation, asked for RCA and SLA credit. logged next steps.
maya: follow-up: i'll open PR to add automated eviction when shard skew > threshold, and a metric emitted to pager if skew persists > 5m.
jake: thumbs up. I'll document the temporary knobs we toggled and timeline. please drop any remaining logs or commands here for the postmortem.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED #1959993333 - status: mitigated at 1959994510. summary: hotpatch fixed shard hashing + eviction cap, continuous-batch autoscale disabled, customer traffic rerouted as needed. follow-up: postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
iris: thanks everyone — we'll meet tomorrow 10am to go over the postmortem and make the fixes permanent.
